4	    "path": "apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/library/reconcile/reconcile-dialog.tsx",
5	    "line": 213,
6	    "finding": "👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡🐛 **Consider · bug: Dragging to select a file name now toggles the row (confidence medium)**\n\nThe row's `onClick` fires for any click whose target isn't the input. That includes the click Chromium sends after a drag-select when mousedown and mouseup both land inside the `<li>`. Someone who drags over `.rowNow` or `.rowAfter` to copy a long file name will untick (or re-tick) that row as a side effect. The change does show on screen (dimmed row, strikethrough, a different summary count and button label), but it's easy to miss after a copy. One fix is to skip the toggle when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty. Another is to add `user-select: none` to `.rowSelectable`, if copying names isn't something users need.\n\n<!-- wachi:finding -->",
7	    "replies": [
8	      {
9	        "author": "csdev19",
10	        "body": "Real, fixed in 59f6d481: the row's click handler returns early when `window.getSelection()` has text, so a drag-select over a name to copy it no longer toggles the row. The test now selects text, clicks the row and checks the box keeps its state. Kept text selectable rather than `user-select: none`, because copying long file names is useful here."
11	      }
12	    ]
13	  }
14	]

tool_use_result.content: 2:import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

findings.title: Spy restore is not guaranteed if the assertion fails
findings.body: `selection.mockRestore()` runs after `expect(box).toBeChecked()` at line 373. If that assertion throws, the `getSelection` mock stays installed for the rest of the file, and later tests would fail for an unrelated reason. Restore it in `afterEach` or in a `try/finally`. The `afterEach` in this file's `vitest` import is already available.

contracts.action: Click on a selectable finding row now skips the toggle when the page has a non-empty text selection
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing row onClick in the same handler, which toggles via setFixing unless the target is inside an input
contracts.before_after: Before: any non-input click toggled the row, including the click that ends a drag-select over a file name. After: a click with non-empty window.getSelection() returns early and does not toggle. The input-target check at line 214 still runs first, so the checkbox's own onChange toggles only once.
contracts.visible_effect: Dragging over a name to copy it no longer unticks the row. A plain click collapses any prior selection on mousedown, so a normal click still toggles.
contracts.failure_mode: window.getSelection() can return null; optional chaining makes that fall through to the toggle. No async work, so there is no rejection or timeout path.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. The row's click handler now returns early when `window.getSelection()?.toString()` is non-empty (`reconcile-dialog.tsx:216`). It runs after the input-target check, so the checkbox still toggles once. The test mocks a selection, clicks the row, and asserts the box keeps its state.

input.summary: The selection guard in the row click handler fixes the earlier drag-select issue, and I found no defects in the production change. One minor test-hygiene note: the `getSelection` spy is restored inline, so a failing assertion would leak the mock into later tests.
